prompt: A nine-person scheduling startup has six multi-site dental groups paying for pilots. Founder-led outreach and onboarding produced all six. At the pilot sites, 70% of invited office managers start setup, 35% complete the practice-management integration, and 22% still schedule through the product in week eight. The two retained groups refer peers and praise the support, but the four others report integration delays and confusing setup. A reseller offers access to 400 dental groups if the startup commits to a trade-show launch and reseller campaign next month; price and reseller economics are not settled. Procurement and integration take six to eight weeks. The CEO wants to accept, hire three salespeople, and optimize demos. Give a 60-day acquisition, activation, retention, and ownership plan.
criteria: Makes acquiring-and-growing-users primary after paid pilot commitment, identifies integration-limited activation and retained value—not lead volume—as the binding growth constraint, and records enterprise evidence latency plus company, product, and survival assumptions.

Maps the complete source-to-retention loop for one dental-group beachhead, defines an activation event tied to completed integration and experienced scheduling value, segments cohorts by source and implementation state, and states causal rivals for setup and retention failure.

Keeps founder-led recruitment, onboarding, and support at the binding point; sends setup artifact and exposure changes to shipping, integration machinery to engineering, and price or reseller economics to designing-business-models before scaling the reseller channel.

Uses explicit numerator/denominator cohort measures for setup, integration, retained scheduling, referral, support, time, and cost over the six-to-eight-week evidence window, with a calendar review, precommitted thresholds, and keep-manual, repair, scale, and stop branches.

Caps the trade-show, reseller, and hiring expansion until activation, retention, support burden, economics, and accountable user effects improve together; does not treat pipeline, demos, praise, starts, or referrals alone as permission to scale.
